t:
Section 32 of the Act of June 25, 1948, chapter 646, 62 Stat. 991, is amended to read as follows:


“Sec. 32. 

(a) 
All laws of the United States in force on September 1, 1948, in which reference is made to a ‘circuit court of appeals’; ‘senior circuit judge’; ‘senior district judge’; ‘presiding judge’; ‘chief justice’, except when reference to the Chief Justice of the United States is intended; or ‘justice’, except when used with respect to a justice of the Supreme Court of the United States in his capacity as such or as a circuit justice, are hereby amended by substituting ‘court of appeals’ for ‘circuit court of appeals’; ‘chief judge of the circuit’ for ‘senior circuit judge’; ‘chief judge of the district court’ for ‘senior district judge’; ‘chief judge’ for ‘presiding judge’; ‘chief judge’ for ‘chief justice’, except when reference to the Chief Justice of the United States is intended; and ‘judge’ for ‘justice’, except when the latter term is used with respect to a justice of the Supreme Court of the United States in his capacity as such or as a circuit justice.


“(b)
All laws of the United States in force on September 1, 1948, in which reference is made to the Supreme Court of the District of Columbia or to the District Court of the United States for the District of Columbia are amended by substituting ‘United States District Court for the District of Columbia’ for such designations.


“(c) 
All laws of the United States in force on September 1, 1948, in which reference is made to the ‘Conference of Senior Circuit Judges’, or to the ‘Judicial Conference of Senior Circuit Judges’ are amended by substituting ‘Judicial Conference of the United States’ for such designations.


“(d) 
This section shall not be construed to amend historical references to courts or judicial offices which have no present or future application to such courts or offices.”.

fable.w: The section only makes terminology substitutions in existing laws, renaming courts, judicial offices, and the Judicial Conference. The word 'Conference' might suggest a consultative body, but it is just the name of a body of federal judges, all inside the federal government, and no consultation process is created. No outside party is given any role in, or right to challenge, a federal decision.
fable.s: are amended by substituting ‘Judicial Conference of the United States’ for such designations

qwen_block.w: This section is purely technical and administrative, amending statutory language to update the names of federal courts and judicial officers (e.g., changing 'circuit court of appeals' to 'court of appeals'). It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government. All entities mentioned are part of the federal judiciary.
qwen_block.s: All laws of the United States in force on September 1, 1948, in which reference is made to a ‘circuit court of appeals’; ‘senior circuit judge’; ‘senior district judge’; ‘presiding judge’; ‘chief justice’, except when reference to the Chief Justice of the United States is intended; or ‘justice’, except when used with respect to a justice of the Supreme Court of the United States in his capacity as such or as a circuit justice, are hereby amended by substituting ‘court of appeals’ for ‘circuit court of appeals’; ‘chief judge of the circuit’ for ‘senior circuit judge’; ‘chief judge of the district court’ for ‘senior district judge’; ‘chief judge’ for ‘presiding judge’; ‘chief judge’ for ‘chief justice’, except when reference to the Chief Justice of the United States is intended; and ‘judge’ for ‘justice’

opus.w: The section only replaces old names for courts and judicial offices with new ones in existing laws. No one outside the federal government is consulted, and there is no hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue. The mention of the 'Judicial Conference' is a proper-noun rename of a body of federal judges, so it is not a process involving outsiders.
opus.s: are amended by substituting ‘Judicial Conference of the United States’ for such designations.
opus.b: This section only renames things. It updates court and judicial-office names in existing laws. The tempting reading is that "Judicial Conference" sounds like a consultative body, but it is a proper noun for a group of federal judges, all inside the federal government, and the section only changes its name.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment that updates terminology in existing federal laws (e.g., changing 'circuit court of appeals' to 'court of appeals'). It does not establish any new process for consultation, coordination, or participation with entities outside the federal government. The entities mentioned (courts, judges) are part of the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: All laws of the United States in force on September 1, 1948, in which reference is made to a ‘circuit court of appeals’; ‘senior circuit judge’; ‘senior district judge’; ‘presiding judge’; ‘chief justice’, except when reference to the Chief Justice of the United States is intended; or ‘justice’, except when used with respect to a justice of the Supreme Court of the United States in his capacity as such or as a circuit justice, are hereby amended by substituting ‘court of appeals’ for ‘circuit court of appeals’; ‘chief judge of the circuit’ for ‘senior circuit judge’; ‘chief judge of the district court’ for ‘senior district judge’; ‘chief judge’ for ‘presiding judge’; ‘chief judge’ for ‘chief justice’, except when reference to the Chief Justice of the United States is intended; and ‘judge’ for ‘justice’
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "Judicial Conference of the United States" is a body that involves outside parties or that the renaming implies a new participatory process. However, the Judicial Conference is composed of federal judges (inside the government), and this section is purely a technical amendment to update terminology in existing statutes. It does not create any new mechanism for non-federal entities to consult with or participate in federal decision-making.
